title: Rectangles the Procedural Way: Struct + Free Function
prompt_md:
## Goal
C++ before classes: bundle related data in a `struct`, and put the behavior in a separate *free function* that operates on that struct. Model rectangles this way and report each area plus a running total.

## Input
- Line 1: an integer N (1 ≤ N ≤ 100), the number of rectangles.
- Next N lines: two integers `width height` per line.

## Output
- For each rectangle, one line: `Area: <area>`.
- After the last rectangle, one line: `Total: <sum of all areas>`.

## What to build
Define a `Rectangle` struct and a free function `int area(Rectangle r)`; the driver in `main()` reads the input and calls them. This separation of data (the struct) from behavior (the free function) is the procedural style that object-oriented programming will later improve on.

title: Path Length with a Struct and a Free Function
prompt_md:
## Goal
Keep practicing the data-plus-free-function style. Given a path that visits several points, report the Manhattan distance of each step and the total length of the path.

## Input
- Line 1: an integer N (2 ≤ N ≤ 100), the number of points.
- Next N lines: two integers `x y` per line, in visiting order.

## Output
- For each step from one point to the next, one line: `Step: <distance>` (N−1 lines total).
- After the last step, one line: `Total: <sum of step distances>`.

The Manhattan distance between (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) is |x1 − x2| + |y1 − y2|.

## What to build
Define a `Point` struct and a free function `int manhattan(Point a, Point b)`. The driver reads points one at a time (it never stores them all at once) and calls your function on each consecutive pair.
